 Microsoft's massive outage enters day two, takes ChatGPT and Claude connectors down with it
 ISN Team 
 13 Nov 2026 
 16:46
 IST Follow Us
 New Update Microsoft's cloud outage, which is now in its second day, has broken the  Microsoft 365 connectors inside ChatGPT and Claude, cutting the AI assistants built by OpenAI and Anthropic off from users' work email, calendars and documents.
 Advertisment Both companies have open, unresolved incidents on their status pages and Anthropic points at Microsoft as the cause.
 In fact, thousands of users also reported issues with the Claude.ai chatbot, with many encountering the "Claude is temporarily unavailable" error.
 Claude is Temporarily unavailable!? 
by u/ducgacon222 in claude 
 Even on Downdetector.in , user reports of outages jumped to around 1,500 shortly after 3:00 pm.
 OpenAI opened an incident titled "Elevated errors affecting the Microsoft 365 connector" on its status page at 1:29 pm Eastern time on Thursday, 12 November, listing ChatGPT 's Connectors and Apps component as degraded.
 Anthropic opened an incident with the same title on  its own status page at 17:52 UTC the same day. Microsoft's disruption, which took down Outlook, Teams, SharePoint Online and Copilot in 74 countries according to Downdetector, had begun minutes earlier and was still unresolved on Friday afternoon India time.
 Anthropic's last update on the incident, at 22:23 UTC on Thursday, left no doubt about where the problem sat.
 "This issue is caused by a Microsoft 365 service incident, and mail, calendar and search tools in the Microsoft 365 connector are still failing for most requests," the company said, pointing users to Microsoft's status page for progress.
 A connector is the pipe that lets an AI assistant read a company's own data. Anthropic launched its Microsoft 365 connector in October 2025 for Claude Team and Enterprise customers, letting Claude search SharePoint and OneDrive documents, "access email threads, analyze communications patterns" in Outlook, and search Teams chats and channel discussions.
 The permissions are delegated and read-only, granted through Microsoft Entra, Microsoft's identity service, and an administrator has to switch the connector on before any user can authenticate. None of that helps when Microsoft's servers stop answering.
 What stopped working
 OpenAI said it was investigating an issue in which new connections to Microsoft connectors may be broken and tools are not working as expected. Fifteen hours later the incident was still in the "investigating" state, with no cause or fix posted.
 Anthropic's account was more detailed. It first reported elevated errors and slow responses on requests to mail, SharePoint, Teams chat and calendar, said new connections might not complete, and by 18:34 UTC said it had identified an issue with an upstream provider.
 A later update added that Claude for Outlook, the add-in that puts Claude inside the Outlook window, was also hit. At 21:18 UTC, the AI giant said the upstream provider was restarting affected servers.
 The Claude API, Claude Code and the Claude Console were listed as operational through Thursday, so the damage was confined to the Microsoft-dependent features. Separately, Anthropic opened a fresh incident at 09:58 UTC on Friday and said it was investigating a problem with users authenticating to Claude.ai and Claude Code, with claude.ai showing a major outage. It has not linked that incident to Microsoft.
 The piece of Microsoft that failed
 The service at the centre of the outage is Exchange Online, Microsoft's cloud email platform, which is why so much else went with it.
 Microsoft said users could not reach mailboxes through Outlook on the web, desktop or mobile, with delivery delays, and that Copilot Chat failed to load or to reach email, calendars and files. Planner, To Do, Defender, Purview, SharePoint Online, Power BI and Windows 365 were affected too, while Teams calls and meetings largely kept running.
 Microsoft's investigation pointed to a process responsible for establishing secure connections on affected servers, which became overwhelmed and stopped processing requests.
 The company said the trigger was not a surge in traffic but a drop in the number of servers available to handle it, after machines failed automated health checks. Charles Lamanna, an Executive Vice President at Microsoft, said the outage was not caused by a cybersecurity breach.
 Fixes kept slipping. Microsoft said at one point that changes introduced to improve availability were "not taking as expected", then reported on Friday that it was seeing positive results for server stability after applying an upstream authentication and routing configuration component patch to part of its infrastructure. Administrators are tracking the incident as MO1550821, with mailbox connectivity under EX1550543, on Microsoft's service health page .
 Indian airlines issued email support advisories
 Air India, IndiGo and Akasa Air all issued advisories as the outage ran through the Indian working day. Air India said it was "closely monitoring the ongoing Microsoft outage", that flight operations remained unaffected, and that it had temporarily rerouted its emails.
 "Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails," said IndiGo.
 The airline pushed urgent requests to its 6E Skai assistant on its website and app.
 Akasa Air reported delays to email support and asked customers to call its care centre or use social media. Delhi airport advised passengers to check flight status before travelling.
 A dependency on Microsoft's infrastructure
 For companies that have wired an AI assistant into their email and files, the failure arrived from an unfamiliar direction. The connector failures affected access to Microsoft data. The data it reads became unreachable, so it had nothing to answer a question about a mail thread or a calendar with.
 This is the second cloud failure in about a year to affect services far from the company that caused it. Last month, Amazon Web Services had a disruption in its Northern Virginia region that ran from 11:48 pm to 2:20 pm Pacific time, roughly 14 hours, which  AWS traced to "a latent race condition in the DynamoDB DNS management system" that left an empty address record for a regional endpoint. That one took down websites and apps.
